questions.q: What is Chomsky’s central claim about the mass media?
a: It favors the wealthy and powerful because wealth and power are unevenly divided
It deliberately promotes socialist ideas to weaken large corporations
It is mostly independent and reports without regard to ownership
It focuses on entertainment because audiences reject serious news
questions.why: The overview says an unequal division of wealth and power produces news coverage that favors the upper class.

questions.q: Why do advertiser interests shape what news stations cover?
a: Stations depend on advertising money and avoid upsetting sponsors
Advertisers are legally required to approve every story
Journalists prefer stories that sell products they personally use
Sponsors provide the reporters who write the coverage
questions.why: Lesson 2 explains that stations need sponsorship, so coverage stays biased toward the advertisers’ interests.

questions.q: What happened to the TV network that aired a documentary about corporate malpractice abroad?
a: It lost the advertising funding that had supported it
It was praised for its independence and gained viewers
It was bought by the companies it had criticized
It received a government award for honest reporting
questions.why: Lesson 2 recounts that the documentary made big business look bad and the funder withdrew support.

questions.q: What does the summary say about the “experts” quoted in the news?
a: They are often paid by the powerful and predict no better than anyone else
They are selected for their independence from corporate interests
They are usually academic researchers with no outside funding
They are more accurate than ordinary people at forecasting events
questions.why: Lesson 3 says experts are paid by the rich and are about as good at predicting as the rest of us.

questions.q: How does the summary reinterpret the media’s coverage of Watergate?
a: It served another elite faction rather than genuinely challenging power
It proved that reporters can override their owners’ interests
It was ignored by the public until years after the scandal
It focused on the little guys rather than on powerful figures
questions.why: Lesson 1 argues the coverage was a tool of the Democrats, who wanted to repair their image.
